function.name: calculate_velocity
function.description: Calculate the final velocity of an object in motion given its initial velocity, acceleration and time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity of the object in m/s. This is a float type value.

acceleration.description: The acceleration of the object in m/s^2. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time for which the object is in motion in seconds. This is a float type value.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time data on current movie releases. If you let me know a specific genre, region, or timeframe you’re interested in, I can suggest some popular titles from recent years or help you find resources where you can check the latest releases.
message.reasoning: User asks "What are the latest movie releases?" We need to respond with a list of movies. But we don't have real-time data. We can provide a general answer or ask for clarification. According to policy, we should not hallucinate. We can say we don't have up-to-date info. We can offer to search but no browsing tool. So we should politely explain limitation.
